clue.text: Malaysian capital detaining group linked to a secret doctrine

indicators.note: linked to means the next piece is joined on after
detaining means holding something inside, so the capital keeps the group within it

parts.note: KL is the usual short form of Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia's capital
ABBA, the Swedish pop group

explanation.surface: A news story about the Malaysian capital holding a band suspected of ties to a secret cult.
explanation.walkthrough: KL (Kuala Lumpur) holds ABBA, giving KABBAL, then A is joined on.
explanation.definitionFit: Kabbala is the Jewish mystical tradition, an esoteric body of teaching handed down to initiates.

clue.text: Tangled bird spread out to dry

parts.note: the knot is a wading bird
to ted is to spread out mown grass to dry as hay

explanation.surface: A bird with ruffled feathers laid out in the sun to dry.
explanation.walkthrough: TED is a farming word for turning and spreading hay.
explanation.definitionFit: Knotted hair or string is twisted and snarled, so the word means tangled.

clue.text: Statesman, as it happens, almost bitten by animal

indicators.note: bitten by means held in the jaws, so the piece goes inside

parts.note: a boar is a wild pig

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: live means broadcast as it happens

explanation.surface: A politician, as it turns out, nearly savaged by a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as it happens' reads as a filler phrase, but it is the broadcasting sense of live, as opposed to recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon Bolivar was the South American liberator and political leader.

clue.text: Diviner month, you said, before year's end

indicators.note: before places these pieces ahead of what follows

parts.note: Aug is the abbreviation for August

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the letter sounds like the word

parts.note: the word you, said aloud, is the letter U

indicators.note: end picks out the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of year

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller tells someone which month comes before the year is out.
explanation.definitionFit: An augur was a Roman priest who foretold events from omens, so a seer or prophet.

clue.text: Helping first worker to support Charlie

indicators.note: to support in a down clue means to sit beneath, so these pieces follow

parts.note: a Charlie is a fool in British slang, as is an ass
1st, written IST
an ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: An aide helping the first employee who supports someone named Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a right Charlie' is British for a fool, an ASS; IST stands in for 1st, and in a down clue support means underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistant as an adjective means giving aid, as in an assistant manager.

clue.text: The benefit of not being well?

definitions.text: The benefit of not being well?

parts.words: The benefit of not being well?
parts.note: reads like a musing on the upside of illness, but means the wages paid while off work ill

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark invites the idea of some hidden advantage to illness; the benefit is literal, a payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Money an employer or the state pays a worker who is absent through illness is a welfare benefit.

clue.text: Break bread

definitions.meaning: second meaning: slang for money; an old slang word for loose change, as bread is for cash

explanation.walkthrough: 'Break bread' looks like the phrase for sharing a meal; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Smash means to shatter something, and in old slang also means coins or ready cash.

clue.text: Using which a rider may secure essential cover

definitions.text: Using which a rider may secure essential cover

parts.words: Using which a rider may secure essential cover
parts.note: the essential cover is a helmet, and the rider fastens it under the jaw

explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' sounds like insurance; it is head protection held on by a strap.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap under the jaw fastens a riding or cycling helmet so it stays put.

clue.text: Rustic type of game that's not hard

indicators.note: that's not means the following letter is missing

parts.note: a pheasant is a game bird
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A country type plays a game that is not difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' sounds like a sport; it is game birds, and PHEASANT loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a countryman of humble rank, a farm labourer.

clue.text: Ultimately try to fill barrel up wherein soldiers may go for a dip?

definitions.text: wherein soldiers may go for a dip?

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of each of the next three words

parts.note: last letter of try
last letter of to
last letter of fill

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a cask is a barrel

explanation.surface: Someone tries in the end to fill a barrel in which troops can take a bath.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers are strips of toast dipped into a soft-boiled egg, a British nursery treat; the question mark flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The yolk sac is the membrane holding the yolk, where a toast finger is dunked.

clue.text: Binds broken bobsleigh whose frame has split

indicators.note: broken signals that the remaining letters are smashed up and rearranged
the frame is the outer pair of letters of the word, and they split off, leaving only its inside

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bobsleigh breaks apart after its frame splits, a racing mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the outer B and H from BOBSLEIGH to leave OBSLEIG, then rearrange those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To oblige someone is to put them under an obligation, constraining them as a duty does.

clue.text: Former lady's maid advanced with considerable trouble

parts.note: big means considerable
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A one-time servant got ahead only after a great deal of difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: The name comes from Abigail in a 17th-century play, a waiting gentlewoman; it became a dated term for the role.
explanation.definitionFit: An abigail is an archaic word for a woman who waits on a lady, so the term is now historical.

clue.text: Comrade Victor has converted

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A friend called Victor has switched his political or religious allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of VICTOR plus HAS gives the Russian word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tovarisch is the Russian form of address used in Soviet times, meaning a fellow party member.

clue.text: More than one stretch breaks back

indicators.note: back says the word for breaks is read from right to left

parts.note: snaps means breaks

explanation.surface: Stretching too far, someone's back gives way more than once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like the body part that breaks; it is the signal to read SNAPS the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: Spans are lengths or periods, so the plural matches several stretches of time or distance.

clue.text: Finally weeping, overwhelmed by dreadful air at funeral

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means swallowed up, so the letter sits within the other word

parts.note: dire means dreadful

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the next word

parts.note: last letter of weeping

explanation.surface: Mourners finally break down in tears, overcome by a grim tune at a funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a slow mournful song or lament sung or played at a burial.

clue.text: Slap detective and cryptically murder playwright

parts.note: a private eye is a detective

indicators.note: read cryptically, murder is 'do in', so the next piece is put inside the playwright

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright
to do in is to murder

explanation.surface: A demand to hit a sleuth and kill a dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: Slap is British slang for make-up, not a blow. 'Do in' means murder, and 'cryptically' tells you to read that phrase literally as an instruction to place one piece within the playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye make-up applied to the lids is a kind of cosmetic, and slap is informal for face paint.

clue.text: Area offering the greatest latitude, in a negative sense

definitions.text: Area offering the greatest latitude, in a negative sense

parts.words: Area offering the greatest latitude, in a negative sense
parts.note: latitude here is the geographic measure, and places south of the equator have negative values, the most negative at the far south

explanation.walkthrough: 'Latitude' suggests freedom, so the clue sounds like a place giving people leeway; it is the polar region with the most southerly latitudes.
explanation.definitionFit: The southern polar region reaches down to ninety degrees south, the extreme of negative latitude.

clue.text: Sin and sex repressed by Conservative jurisdiction

indicators.note: repressed by means held down within, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
to err is to sin
it is a slang term for sex

explanation.surface: A Tory government clamps down on sin and sex within its domain.
explanation.definitionFit: A territory is a region under a given authority's control, the area where its power runs.

clue.text: Hip person looking on, but not at, examiner

parts.note: in means fashionable, hip

indicators.note: but not means the following short word is removed from the word before

parts.note: a spectator is someone looking on
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trendy onlooker who is not actually at the scene is somehow an examiner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not at' reads as a comment on where the person is; it is an instruction to remove two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector is an official whose job is to scrutinise and check things.

clue.text: Sea tide briefly changed, trapping old salts

indicators.note: trapping means enclosing the next piece
changed means the letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: briefly means cut short by the last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The sea's tide turns briefly, catching some old sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salts' reads as sailors; it is the chemistry sense. SEA plus TID is rearranged around O.
explanation.definitionFit: Iodates are chemical salts of iodic acid.

clue.text: Allies picking up equipment for those who treat rising cause of death in Asia

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the whole is read upwards, backwards
picking up means taking hold of, so the allies hold the equipment between them

parts.note: UK and US, two allied nations
PPE, personal protective equipment, worn by medical staff

explanation.surface: Allied forces pick up medical gear, with deaths in Asia mounting.
explanation.walkthrough: UK and US surround PPE, and the whole reads bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Seppuku is ritual suicide by disembowelling, practised by Japanese samurai.

clue.text: Nothing must stop academic demonstration

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so the letter goes inside as a stopper

parts.note: prof is short for professor, an academic
O is nought, nothing

explanation.surface: No protest should be allowed to halt a professor's demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demonstration' sounds like a protest march; it is a logical demonstration.
explanation.definitionFit: A proof is a demonstration that something is true, as in mathematics.

clue.text: Melodious harp one played

indicators.note: played suggests music being worked, here the letters being rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A harpist plays a tuneful piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Orphean refers to Orpheus, the legendary musician whose songs charmed even stones, so tuneful.

clue.text: Worthless bits of objects aimed at bolstering fine silver

indicators.note: bolstering means propping up from below, so in a down clue this piece comes after

parts.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
ends are aims or objectives

explanation.surface: Scrap fragments of the targets that were set to prop up good silver.
explanation.walkthrough: A fag is a cigarette in British slang, so fag ends are cigarette stubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Fag ends are leftover scraps or stubs, figuratively the useless remnants of anything.

clue.text: Intensity of final farewell following heart transplant?

indicators.note: the letter at the heart of the word is swapped out for another, as a transplant replaces an organ

parts.note: death is the last farewell of all

explanation.surface: How deeply someone feels a last goodbye after a heart operation.
explanation.walkthrough: DEATH has A at its centre; transplanting it with P gives the answer. The question mark admits that the replacement letter is the setter's whim rather than clued.
explanation.definitionFit: Depth of feeling is its strength, so depth can mean intensity, as of colour or emotion.

clue.text: Subject of test words that may follow French and precede Latin?

parts.note: French Guinea was the colonial name of what is now Guinea
Pig Latin is the children's word game

explanation.surface: A test question asking which words can follow French and go before Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: One word completes French Guinea, the West African colony; the other makes Pig Latin, a children's coded language.
explanation.definitionFit: Something used in an experiment is called a guinea pig, after the rodent once used in laboratories.

clue.text: Visitor all but seconds judge

indicators.note: all but means everything except the last letter

parts.note: a guest is a visitor

explanation.surface: A visitor who almost judges for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To guess is to estimate, forming an opinion without full knowledge.

clue.text: Source of down clue I derived to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A self-referential remark that a down clue was partly worked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like a direction in the grid; it is feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider duck plucks soft feathers from its breast to line its nest, the source of eiderdown.

clue.text: Edges of nail-head left in flat wheel

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the next word

parts.note: true means level or flat, as a surface trued up

indicators.note: edges are the outside letters of the word, its first and last

parts.note: first and last letters of nail-head

explanation.surface: A carpenter sees the sides of a nail head poking from a flat bicycle wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat wheel' reads as a punctured tyre, but 'flat' gives TRUE and 'wheel' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A trundle is a small wheel or castor, as under a trundle bed.

clue.text: Roland endlessly bored by dame's male friend

indicators.note: bored by means pierced, with the next piece driven into the middle
endlessly means the name loses both its end letters

parts.note: taken as written, before its ends are cut
DBE, Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire, is the honour a dame holds

explanation.surface: A man named Roland finds himself wearied by a lady's boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bored' suggests tedium but means drilled into. A dame in Britain holds the DBE honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Old bean is a dated British form of address to a chum, a familiar term for a pal.

clue.text: Complaints made by short thick wife and kids on vacation

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: squat means short and thick in build

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: first and last letters of kids

explanation.surface: A grumble about a stocky wife and children away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' suggests a holiday, but it means the word is vacated, emptied of its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Squawks are loud raucous protests, an informal word for grievances voiced noisily.

clue.text: Try on extremely stiff new pants

indicators.note: new signals the letters are put into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: extremely picks the extreme letters, the first and last, of the next word

parts.note: first and last letters of stiff

explanation.surface: Advice to try on some stiff new underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants are underpants in British usage, not trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Y-fronts are a style of men's briefs, and in British English pants means underwear.
